subject: Hosted API p99 surge & customer escalation — Shopline impact / status + postmortem
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@shopline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:21 -0800
Subject: Urgent: orders failing / p99 latency spike since 08:40 PT

Hi Marissa / Markus —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency on the Redwood Hosted API starting ~08:40 PT this morning. The behavior started as timeouts for 2–3% of our CreateCompletion calls and escalated into intermittent 503s and higher-than-expected tail latency. Impact: shoppers unable to complete checkout on a subset of our high-concurrency endpoints.

Quick facts from our side:
- Errors: 503 / timeout spikes across three regions (us-west most affected)
- p95 went from ~120ms to ~1.5s and p99 to ~3.2s for text-generation route
- Request rate steady; we did not push a traffic spike on our side

We need immediate confirmation this is on Redwood infrastructure and an estimate for mitigation. Our ops lead (ops@shopline.com) is standing by.

Please escalate — this is affecting revenue.

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Director of Platform Engineering, Shopline

Subject: Re: Urgent: orders failing / p99 latency spike since 08:40 PT

Quick triage notes (initial):

- Confirmed: our telemetry shows a p95/p99 increase starting 08:38–08:42 PT in us-west. Errors correlate with queueing in the serving layer and an uptick in model kv-cache misses for a popular model variant (gptx-7b-q4).
- Root-suspect: a combination of an unbalanced autoscaling event + a recent kernel selection change that increased cold-path latency for certain sequence-length distributions. We also saw a small memory-edge case that caused some worker restarts (not a full node termination).
- Immediate mitigation applied at 09:25 PT: rolled back the kernel selector flag for affected pool and bumped the pre-warm pool size for dedicated shared capacity. Observed p95 improvement in staging; beginning to see customer p95 drop but p99 still elevated for heavy tails.

Next steps (short):
1) Continue rollback monitoring for 30m and gradually restore kernels if stable.
2) Add temporary routing policy: route Shopline traffic to a warm pool variant (latency-optimized model) as a fallback. Need ops help to apply policy.
3) Capture heap/trace dumps for affected workers (attached sample).
4) Draft status page message for customers and a short exec update.

I’ll attach the initial metrics CSV and a heap screenshot.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: DRAFT: Status update — Partial service degradation impacting response tail latency

Hi Sarah —

Thank you for the patience. Below is a short status update we intend to publish to the Redwood status page and share with your ops team. Please let me know if anything here is inaccurate.

Status (10:05 PT): Partial degradation detected for Hosted API (text-generation endpoints) in us-west. We observed increased p95/p99 latency and a small fraction of 503 responses affecting a subset of customers, including Shopline.

Impact: Customers experienced higher-than-normal tail latency; a subset of requests returned 503s/timeouts. Not all customers were affected; spike concentrated on models using gptx-7b-q4 and long sequence lengths.

Mitigation: We applied an immediate rollback of a recent kernel selector change and activated a warm-pool fallback for affected traffic. Early telemetry shows p95 improving; we continue to monitor p99 tail.

Next updates: We will post another update at 10:35 PT or sooner if the situation changes.

Root cause (initial): Suspected regression in kernel selector + autoscaler interaction causing worker cold-path latency and transient restarts. Full RCA pending.

Contact: status@redwood.ai for updates.

—Jordan Blake
Head of Technical Communications, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 13:18:45 -0800
Subject: Incident follow-up: findings, remediation, and action items

Team —

Post-incident summary (findings):
- Root cause: an experiment in kernel selection logic introduced a slower cold-path for customers using gptx-7b-q4 with variable long sequences. The slower path, combined with an autoscaler threshold tuned too narrowly, allowed queueing and a handful of worker restarts that amplified the tail.
- Why it affected Shopline: their workload has a high variance in sequence length and sustained mid-level concurrency; routing put them into an affected shared pool.

Remediation completed:
1) Reverted kernel selection change (rolled back 09:25 PT 2026-03-02).
2) Increased autoscaler headroom and extended pre-warm pool time; these are rolled to prod-systems as hotfixes.
3) Added an emergency routing policy to direct sensitive accounts to the latency-optimized variant.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Dev: add a pre-merge perf test for kernel selector changes (ETA 2026-03-09)
- Ev (SRE): tune autoscaler thresholds and add a canary ramp policy (ETA 2026-03-10)
- Jordan: publish final incident postmortem and customer-friendly summary (ETA 2026-03-04)
- Marissa / CS: prepare commercial credit proposal for Shopline and coordinate acceptance (ETA 2026-03-06)

Attachments: incident-digest-draft.docx (draft postmortem), p95-report-2026-03-02.csv

We should also prepare a short executive one-pager for leadership that highlights business impact and remediation timeline — Markus, I can draft if you want.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
